title: The Hierarchical Nonprofit
description: The hierarchical nonprofit — the traditional pyramid — structures: the board (the governance), the CEO/ED (the executive), the directors (the functions — the programs, the development, the finance, the operations), the managers (the teams), and the staff (the delivery). The strengths: the clarity (the everyone knows the boss — the decisions), the accountability (the chain — the responsible), the scalability (the layers added — the growth), and the funder comfort (the familiar — the credible). The failure modes: the rigidity (the slow — the bureaucratic), the distance (the leadership from the mission — the frontline), and the silos (the functions — the uncoordinated). The disciplines: the delegation (the real — the empowered), the communication (the up and down — the flowing), and the mission proximity (the leaders in the field — the grounded). The fit: the large service-delivery nonprofits — the clarity needed, the scale managed.
key_points: Board, CEO, directors, managers, staff: the pyramid
Disciplines: delegate, communicate, stay close to mission
how_it_works: Define layers, delegate truly, communicate vertically, keep leaders field-connected.

title: When Hierarchy Helps and Harms
description: Hierarchy’s fit — the when — decides: helps when the scale demands coordination (the hundreds of staff — the organized), the compliance demands control (the regulated services — the accountable), the crisis demands command (the emergency — the decisive); harms when the work demands creativity (the innovation — the stifled), the mission demands agility (the changing needs — the slow), the people demand voice (the professionals — the infantilized). The hybrid answer: the hierarchy for the accountabilities (the clear), the networks for the work (the collaborative), the mission for the alignment (the shared). The disciplines: the hierarchy audit (the layers — the necessary?), the empowerment (the decisions pushed down — the owned), and the feedback (the upward — the heard). The principle: the structure serves the mission — the hierarchy where it helps, the freedom where it harms.
key_points: Hybrid: hierarchy for accountability, networks for work
how_it_works: Assess needs, keep necessary layers, empower decisions downward, hear upward feedback.

title: The Flat Organization
description: The flat organization — the minimal-hierarchy — structures: the collective (the all — the deciding), the roles (the rotating or the elected — the functional), the consensus or consent (the decisions — the together), and the minimal administration (the shared — the distributed). The strengths: the equality (the everyone’s voice — the democratic), the agility (the fast — the unbureaucratic), the engagement (the ownership — the deep), and the mission alignment (the shared — the lived). The failure modes: the tyranny of structurelessness (the Jo Freeman — the informal power — the unaccountable), the decision paralysis (the consensus — the slow), and the scale ceiling (the dozens — the limit). The disciplines: the explicit structure (the roles written — the tyranny prevented), the decision rules (the consent — the efficient), and the conflict (the surfaced — the resolved). The fit: the small, the values-driven, the collaborative — the dozens, not the hundreds.
key_points: Failure: structurelessness tyranny, paralysis, scale ceiling
Disciplines: explicit roles, consent rules, surfaced conflict
how_it_works: Write roles explicitly, decide by consent, surface conflict, rotate power, respect scale limits.

title: Flat Done Right: The Disciplines
description: Flat organizations that work — the disciplines: the role clarity (the written — the accountabilities; the rotation — the shared), the decision protocols (the domains — the who-decides-what; the consent — the efficient; the advice — the consulted), the financial transparency (the open books — the trusted), the conflict system (the mediation — the structured; the restorative — the healing), and the onboarding (the culture — the transmitted). The examples: the worker collectives (the democratic workplaces), the activist groups (the affinity), the small nonprofits (the mission teams). The maintenance: the regular retrospectives (the process — the improved), the power audit (the informal — the named), and the growth decision (the scale — the structured or the split). The principle: the flat is the disciplined — the structurelessness is the failure, not the flatness.
how_it_works: Clarify roles, protocol decisions, open finances, structure conflict, audit power, retrospective regularly.

title: The Network Organization
description: The network organization — the nodes and the hub — structures: the members/nodes (the autonomous — the self-governing), the hub (the minimal — the coordinating, not the commanding), the protocols (the shared — the membership, the brand, the decisions), and the flows (the knowledge — the circulated; the resources — the pooled where apt). The strengths: the scale (the viral growth), the resilience (the node failures — the absorbed), the innovation (the edge — the experiments), and the lightness (the minimal overhead). The failure modes: the incoherence (the no-protocols — the chaos), the hub capture (the coordinator’s empire), and the free-riding (the takers — the givers exhausted). The disciplines: the protocols (the explicit — the enforced kindly), the hub discipline (the lean — the serving), and the value (the circulated — the recognized). The fit: the movements, the alliances, the distributed missions — the many, the autonomous.
key_points: Disciplines: explicit protocols, lean hub, circulated value
how_it_works: Recruit nodes, write protocols, fund lean hub, circulate knowledge, enforce kindly.

title: The Federated Structure
description: The federated structure — the detailed architecture — balances: the national (the brand — the standards — the shared services — the advocacy), the regionals (the coordination — the support — where apt), the locals (the delivery — the fundraising — the community), and the constitution (the affiliation agreements — the powers reserved per level — the money flows — the dispute resolution). The variants: the tightly-coupled (the standards-heavy — the brand-controlled), the loosely-coupled (the network-like — the autonomous), and the hybrid (the core standards — the local freedom). The economics: the dues up (the national funded), the services down (the chapters supported), the local retained (the incentive). The governance: the chapter representation (the voice), the national board (the balanced), the assemblies (the sovereign). The principle: the federation is the negotiated balance — the unity and the autonomy, the standards and the freedom.
key_points: Constitution: powers, money, disputes per level
how_it_works: Write the constitution, fund flows both ways, represent chapters, calibrate coupling, resolve disputes.

title: The Chapter Structure (Detailed)
description: The chapter structure — the local-entity architecture — details: the legal (the separate incorporation — the liability; the group exemption — the IRS; the affiliation — the agreement), the governance (the local board — the elected; the bylaws — the aligned; the reporting — the upward), the operations (the programming — the local; the finances — the managed; the compliance — the ensured), and the relationship (the support — the received; the dues — the paid; the brand — the licensed). The lifecycle: the organizing (the chartered), the growing (the supported), the mature (the contributing), the struggling (the intervened), the closing (the dignified). The disciplines: the legal compliance (the filings — the current), the financial integrity (the audited where apt), and the mission alignment (the standards — the upheld). The failure: the chapter as the fiefdom — the unaccountable. The principle: the chapter is the mission local — the empowered, the supported, the accountable.
key_points: Lifecycle managed: charter to dignified close
how_it_works: Charter legally, govern locally, operate to standards, support actively, manage lifecycle.

title: The Collective Structure
description: The collective — the worker/member-owned — structures: the membership (the owners — the workers or the community), the democracy (the one-member-one-vote — the sovereign), the management (the elected or the rotating — the accountable; the hired managers — the supervised), and the economics (the surplus — the shared or the reinvested; the wages — the equitable). The forms: the worker cooperative (the employees own), the consumer cooperative (the customers own — the credit unions, the food co-ops), the producer cooperative (the producers — the agricultural, the artisan), and the multi-stakeholder (the hybrid). The strengths: the democracy (the owned), the equity (the shared), the resilience (the member-loyal), and the mission lock (the owned — the unsellable). The failure modes: the slow decisions (the democratic — the deliberate), the capital constraints (the member-funded — the limited), and the professional gaps (the expertise — the hired). The disciplines: the business rigor (the cooperative is the business — the managed), the democratic culture (the participated), and the education (the cooperative principles — the taught).
key_points: Strengths: democracy, equity, resilience, mission lock
Disciplines: business rigor, democratic culture, education
how_it_works: Incorporate cooperatively, capitalize via members, govern democratically, manage rigorously, educate continuously.

title: The Cooperative in Depth
description: Cooperatives — the detailed — operate on the seven principles (the ICA: voluntary membership, democratic control, member economic participation, autonomy, education, cooperation among cooperatives, concern for community): the governance (the board elected — the one-member-one-vote; the management — the hired, the supervised), the capital (the member shares — the limited return; the retained surplus — the indivisible reserves), and the operations (the business — the competitive; the member benefit — the primary). The scale: the global movement (the millions of members — the credit unions, the agricultural co-ops, the Mondragon). The disciplines: the member engagement (the participated — the democratic), the professional management (the hired — the accountable), and the cooperative advantage (the member loyalty — the trust). The failure: the cooperative in name only — the democratic forms, the managerial reality. The principle: the cooperative is the business owned by its people — the principles lived, the business run.
key_points: Member shares; limited return; indivisible reserves
how_it_works: Incorporate on principles, capitalize via members, elect boards, hire managers, engage members, cooperate.

title: The Movement Structure
description: Movements — the large-scale change structures — organize: the narrative (the story — the compelling; the identity — the shared), the nodes (the organizations — the autonomous; the individuals — the mobilized), the coordination (the light — the convening, not the commanding; the moments — the synchronized), and the power (the numbers — the demonstrated; the disruption — the leveraged; the narrative — the shifted). The theories: the resource mobilization (the organized), the political process (the opportunities — the seized), the framing (the storied), and the distributed (the leaderful — the many leaders). The disciplines: the inclusivity (the broad — the powerful), the nonviolence (the principled or the strategic), and the sustainability (the marathon — the paced). The failure: the moment without the movement — the viral, the vanished. The principle: the movement is the people’s power organized — the storied, the structured lightly, the sustained.
key_points: Narrative plus nodes plus light coordination
how_it_works: Tell the story, grow nodes, coordinate lightly, synchronize moments, sustain inclusively.

title: Structure Selection: The Fit Framework
description: Choosing structure — the fit framework — assesses: the mission (the service delivery — the hierarchical; the advocacy — the network; the democracy — the cooperative), the scale (the dozens — the flat; the hundreds — the hierarchical; the thousands — the federated), the people (the professionals — the empowered; the volunteers — the coordinated; the members — the represented), the environment (the stable — the structured; the turbulent — the adaptive), and the values (the democratic — the participatory; the efficient — the directed). The hybrid reality: the organizations combine (the hierarchical core — the networked edges — the movement moments). The disciplines: the fit reviewed (the structure — the evolving), the transitions (the managed — the communicated), and the honesty (the structure — the actual, not the chart). The principle: the structure serves the mission and the people — the fit, not the fashion.
key_points: Mission, scale, people, environment, values: the fit factors
how_it_works: Assess fit factors, choose or hybridize, implement, review as conditions change.

title: The Matrix Organization (Nonprofit Edition)
description: The matrix — the dual-reporting structure — adapts for mission organizations: the dimensions (the functions — the programs, the development, the finance; the geographies or populations — the regions, the communities; the projects — the initiatives), the roles (the dual-reporting staff — the clarity needed; the dimension leads — the negotiated), and the governance (the conflicts — the escalated clearly; the priorities — the aligned). The strengths: the multidimensional (the complex missions — the served), the resource sharing (the expertise — the pooled), and the collaboration (the silos — the bridged). The failure modes: the confusion (the two bosses — the conflicted), the slowness (the negotiated — the delayed), and the power struggles (the dimensions — the warring). The disciplines: the role clarity (the RACI — the explicit), the conflict protocol (the escalated — the resolved), and the culture (the collaborative — the required). The fit: the complex, the multi-site, the multi-program — the managed multidimensionally.
key_points: Disciplines: RACI clarity, conflict protocol, collaborative culture
how_it_works: Define dimensions, clarify dual roles, protocol conflicts, align priorities, culture collaboration.

title: Holacracy for Mission Organizations
description: Holacracy — the constitutional self-management — adapts for nonprofits: the constitution (the rules — the adopted), the circles (the teams — the nested; the roles — the defined), the governance meetings (the roles evolved — the tensions processed), the tactical meetings (the work — the triaged), and the lead links (the accountabilities — the assigned). The nonprofit adaptations: the board retained (the fiduciary — the legal; the holacracy — the operational), the mission anchor (the purpose — the circle’s; the mission — the ultimate), and the volunteer circles (the defined roles — the bounded). The strengths: the clarity (the explicit), the agility (the distributed authority), and the engagement (the empowered). The failure modes: the constitutional heaviness (the process — the burdened), the cultural mismatch (the hierarchical habits — the persistent), and the board confusion (the governance — the blurred). The disciplines: the training (the invested), the coaching (the supported), and the patience (the 18-month — the adoption). The fit: the adaptive, the engaged, the willing — the few.
key_points: Board retained for fiduciary; holacracy for operations
how_it_works: Adopt constitution, form circles, define roles, run meetings, train deeply, anchor to mission.

title: Sociocracy in Community Organizations
description: Sociocracy — the consent-based governance — suits community organizations: the circles (the teams — the domains; the double-linking — the connected), the consent (the decisions — the no-objection; the objections — the reasoned, the resolved), the elections (the sociocratic — the nominated, the consented), and the aims (the circle’s — the defined). The strengths: the equivalence (the every-voice — the heard), the effectiveness (the consent — the efficient), and the transparency (the open). The community fit: the values-aligned (the participatory), the small-to-medium (the dozens), the intentional (the committed). The disciplines: the facilitation (the trained), the objection (the welcomed — the integrated), and the review (the regular — the improved). The failure: the consent as the consensus — the misunderstood, the slow. The principle: the sociocracy is the governance of equals — the consent, the circles, the equivalence.
how_it_works: Form circles, define aims, decide by consent, elect sociocratically, facilitate well, review.

title: The Fiscal Sponsor Structure
description: The fiscal sponsor structure — the incubated — organizes: the sponsor (the 501(c)(3) — the legal; the services — the financial, the compliance, the HR), the projects (the sponsored — the mission-aligned; the agreements — the clear), and the relationship (the oversight — the responsible; the autonomy — the respected). The variants: the comprehensive (the Model A — the owned), the pre-approved grant (the Model C — the independent), and the incubator (the multiple — the cohort). The economics: the fees (the 5–15% — the services), the scale (the many projects — the leveraged), and the sustainability (the sponsor’s — the ensured). The disciplines: the alignment (the missions — the fit), the clarity (the agreements — the explicit), and the graduation (the planned — the supported). The failure: the sponsor as the landlord — the extracted, not the incubated. The principle: the sponsorship is the mission’s nursery — the sheltered, the grown, the graduated.
key_points: Sponsor provides legal status and back-office
Models A, C, and incubator variants
how_it_works: Align missions, agree clearly, oversee responsibly, support growth, graduate on plan.

title: The Coalition Structure
description: The coalition structure — the alliance architecture — organizes: the members (the organizations — the autonomous; the agreement — the signed), the governance (the steering committee — the representative; the decision rules — the clear; the staff — the minimal), the work (the workstreams — the divided; the campaigns — the joint), and the resources (the dues — the pooled; the grants — the joint; the in-kind — the contributed). The disciplines: the shared purpose (the real — the binding), the equity (the small voiced — the large restrained), and the coordination (the funded — the staffed). The lifecycle: the formation (the energized), the campaigning (the active), the winning (the celebrated), the sustaining or sunsetting (the honest). The failure: the coalition of the unwilling — the signed, the absent. The principle: the coalition is the power pooled — the structured lightly, the managed actively.
how_it_works: Recruit around purpose, agree principles, staff lightly, work in streams, sustain or sunset honestly.

title: The Social Franchise Structure
description: The social franchise — the replication with quality — structures: the franchisor (the model owner — the codified; the support — the training, the brand, the systems), the franchisees (the local operators — the mission-aligned; the agreements — the standards, the fees, the territory), and the quality (the monitoring — the measured; the accreditation — the earned; the de-franchising — the last resort). The economics: the fees (the affordable — the sustainable), the local fundraising (the retained — the incentivized), and the scale (the replicated — the quality-held). The strengths: the rapid scale (the proven model — the spread), the local ownership (the invested), and the quality (the systematized). The failure modes: the quality dilution (the growth — the unsupervised), the franchisee failure (the unsupported — the collapsed), and the mission drift (the profitable — the off-mission). The disciplines: the codification (the manual — the complete), the selection (the vetted), and the support (the continuous). The examples: the replicated programs — the proven models spread.
key_points: Franchisor owns codified model; franchisees operate locally
how_it_works: Codify the model, select franchisees, train and support, monitor quality, scale deliberately.

title: The Merger Structure: Post-Deal Architecture
description: Post-merger structure — the combined architecture — designs: the integration (the systems — the merged; the cultures — the blended; the brands — the decided), the leadership (the combined — the selected; the redundant — the transitioned kindly), the governance (the board — the merged; the representation — the balanced), and the operations (the programs — the rationalized; the back-office — the consolidated; the locations — the optimized). The disciplines: the integration plan (the 100-day — the detailed), the culture (the deliberately built — the new), and the communication (the constant — the honest). The failure: the merger on paper — the unintegrated, the cultures warring. The principle: the merger’s value is the integration — the designed, the led, the completed.
how_it_works: Plan integration, select leadership, merge systems, blend cultures, communicate, complete.

title: The Backbone Structure (Collective Impact)
description: The backbone structure — the collective’s infrastructure — organizes: the backbone entity (the dedicated — the neutral; the staffed — the facilitative), the steering (the cross-sector — the representative; the decisions — the shared), the workgroups (the aligned activities — the divided), and the community (the engaged — the voiced). The funding: the multi-year (the committed — the philanthropic; the public — the aligned), the backbone’s own (the sustained — the ensured). The disciplines: the neutrality (the agenda held — the not set), the data (the shared measurement — the built), and the adaptation (the emergent — the managed). The failure: the backbone as the boss — the directed, not the facilitated. The principle: the backbone is the collective’s servant — the structured, the funded, the humble.
how_it_works: Establish neutral backbone, fund multi-year, convene steering, build measurement, facilitate emergence.

title: Structural Evolution: Growing and Changing
description: Structural evolution — the organization’s changing form — follows: the triggers (the scale — the outgrown; the strategy — the shifted; the crisis — the forced), the options (the restructured — the redesigned; the federated — the distributed; the merged — the combined; the sunset — the concluded), the process (the assessed — the honestly; the designed — the participatorily; the transitioned — the supported), and the landing (the new — the stabilized; the evaluated — the learned). The disciplines: the honesty (the need — the named), the participation (the affected — the involved), and the support (the transitioned — the cared for). The failure: the reorganization as the ritual — the boxes redrawn, the work unchanged. The principle: the structure evolves with the mission — the honest assessment, the participatory design, the supported transition.
how_it_works: Name the need, involve the affected, design participatorily, transition supportively, evaluate.

title: The All-Volunteer Structure
description: The all-volunteer structure — the detailed — organizes: the working board (the governing — the doing; the officers — the leading), the committees (the work — the distributed; the chaired — the accountable), the members (the participating — the recruited; the recognized), and the minimal staff (the none or the fractional — the supplemented). The economics: the dues and donations (the lean), the in-kind (the donated), the pro-bono (the professional gaps filled). The lifecycle: the founding (the energized), the institutionalizing (the systematized), the renewing or declining (the honest). The disciplines: the distribution (the work spread — the burnout prevented), the documentation (the knowledge — the captured), and the joy (the fun — the sustained). The failure: the heroic few — the burned out, the collapsed. The principle: the all-volunteer is the mission’s purest structure — the distributed, the documented, the joyful.
how_it_works: Distribute via committees, document everything, supplement professionally, prevent burnout, celebrate.

title: The Hybrid Organization
description: The hybrid — the nonprofit/for-profit blend — structures: the pair (the nonprofit — the mission; the for-profit — the enterprise; the relationship — the defined), the shared (the brand — the licensed; the leadership — the overlapping carefully; the resources — the allocated fairly), and the governance (the boards — the separate; the conflicts — the managed; the IRS — the compliant). The economics: the enterprise funding the mission (the sustained), the mission legitimizing the enterprise (the branded). The disciplines: the separation (the legal — the respected), the fairness (the transactions — the arm’s-length), and the mission lock (the protected). The failure: the tangle — the undocumented, the conflicted, the penalized. The principle: the hybrid is the both/and — the structured cleanly, the mission protected.
key_points: Nonprofit plus for-profit pair; defined relationship
Enterprise funds mission; mission legitimizes enterprise
how_it_works: Form both entities, define relationship, separate governance, transact arm’s-length, comply.

title: The Platform Organization
description: The platform organization — the digital-age structure — organizes: the platform (the technology — the connecting; the rules — the governing), the participants (the many — the contributing; the roles — the varied), the core (the minimal staff — the maintaining; the curating), and the governance (the community — the moderated; the policies — the enforced fairly). The economics: the scale (the near-zero marginal cost), the network effects (the value growing with participants), and the sustainability (the freemium, the services, the grants — the mixed). The disciplines: the trust (the safety — the designed), the moderation (the fair — the transparent), and the openness (the API — the ecosystem). The failure: the ghost platform — the built, the unpopulated. The principle: the platform is the infrastructure for the mission’s many — the built well, the governed fairly, the populated deliberately.
key_points: Network effects as the growth engine
how_it_works: Build platform, seed participants, govern community, moderate fairly, sustain via mixed revenue.

title: The Sunset Structure: Closing Well
description: The sunset — the intentional closing — structures the end: the decision (the board’s — the mission-accomplished or the mission-unviable; the honest), the plan (the timeline — the 6–12 months; the obligations — the honored: the staff, the clients, the funders, the creditors), the assets (the distributed — the cy pres: the mission-adjacent; the records — the archived), and the legacy (the lessons — the published; the people — the transitioned; the celebration — the deserved). The disciplines: the honesty (the reasons — the stated), the care (the people — the supported), and the compliance (the dissolutions — the filed; the final 990). The failure: the zombie — the undead, the draining. The principle: the well-closed organization honors its mission — the intentional end is the success, not the failure.
key_points: Board decision: mission accomplished or unviable
Lessons published; people transitioned; legacy celebrated
how_it_works: Decide honestly, plan the wind-down, honor people and obligations, distribute assets legally, archive legacy.
